# The Water-Stone of the Wise

Indeed, it is even more astonishing that some people seek after this highest art <note>Ecclesiastes 7:23–25 discusses the difficulty of finding wisdom and the reason behind things.</note> and even try to practice it while still doubting its nature. They wonder if it is a natural and truly <term>magical</term> <gloss>natural wisdom or science</gloss> art, or if it is a preternatural and <term>necromantic</term> <gloss>black magic involving the conjuration of spirits</gloss> art that can only be obtained through forbidden spirits and unlawful means. Not at all, my good man! Without divine permission, the Devil and all the ungodly lack the power even to touch the smallest part of this art, much less to master it or practice it at their own whim. By no means, I say; it rests solely in the hand and power of God, who grants it to whom He wills and takes it away again. For into this art—which takes its origin from and out of God—no pleasure-seekers are admitted, much less the dreadful spirits of hell. On the contrary, only such a spirit as is simple, upright, true, constant, and of a pure and pious essence is allowed. However, the modern world—careless and ungodly—does not recognize this spirit. Therefore, the world remains ignorant of its essence and its highest mystery in many things. As soon as people hear anything about it, if they cannot immediately grasp it, these worldly companions <note>Wisdom of Solomon 1:1–5 explains that wisdom will not enter a soul that plots evil or dwell in a body enslaved to sin.</note> call it foolishness. Because of their blindness, that spirit will remain perpetually hidden from them and will eventually be taken from them entirely.

<note>A small ink flourish or doodle consisting of several wavy vertical and horizontal strokes appears in the right margin.</note>

Lest I wander further than is right from my purpose with this discussion, let me return to the point and bring it to a conclusion. Therefore, as a friendly exhortation, I wish to impress this deeply upon pious craftsmen: to the extent that one directs their heart, soul, indeed their life and actions toward God <note>referencing Ecclesiasticus 18 and 29, which emphasize self-examination and keeping the commandments</note>, to that same extent will they perceive a remarkable benefit every day and every hour in the progress of the Stone and their labor. I myself have observed this every day with the greatest diligence and devotion, and I have experienced it to be true in practice. Therefore, from the very beginning, a person ought to direct all their actions toward this goal and prepare themselves so that they may later achieve a successful conclusion in both works <note>the spiritual preparation and the physical laboratory practice</note>.
